title: Networking Foundations
description: Packets, layers as contracts, Ethernet, IP, and the socket a program actually sees. Routing politics wait.

sourceReferences.title: Stanford CS144
sourceReferences.notes: Packets and a reliable byte stream before BGP. Layers as implementation contracts.

sourceReferences.title: End-to-end arguments in system design
sourceReferences.notes: Functions that only the endpoints can implement correctly.

sourceReferences.title: Internet Protocol
sourceReferences.notes: IPv4 addressing, TTL, fragmentation. Mechanism, not RFC trivia.

sourceReferences.title: Domain Names — Concepts and Facilities
sourceReferences.notes: Names that resolve to addresses. The system depth waits.

modules.title: Packets and layers
learningObjectives: Treat layers as contracts, not a morality play
Treat a packet as a header plus a payload that can be lost alone

modules.title: Link and local delivery
learningObjectives: Deliver a frame on a local medium using MAC addresses
Resolve an IP to a MAC before sending on Ethernet

modules.title: Internet Protocol
learningObjectives: Treat an IPv4 address as a hierarchical name routers forward on
Use a prefix length, not a class, to decide the network

modules.title: The host interface
learningObjectives: Bind a port and exchange bytes through the socket API
Resolve a name and borrow an address before a program can talk

concepts.name: The network stack
concepts.summary: Layers as contracts, not a morality play.
objectives: Explain a layer as a contract about what the layer above does not have to know
Name which job belongs to the link, the internet, and the transport, without treating the stack as a morality play

concepts.name: Packets
concepts.summary: A header plus a payload, lost independently of its neighbors.
objectives: Describe a packet as a header plus a payload that can be lost independently of its neighbors
Predict what a receiver can and cannot assume about the next packet

concepts.name: Why layering
concepts.summary: Each layer offers a service and hides a mechanism.
objectives: Explain that each layer offers a service and hides a mechanism
Distinguish a service a layer promises from the mechanism it uses to keep that promise

concepts.name: The end-to-end argument
concepts.summary: Functions that only the endpoints can implement correctly.
objectives: State the end-to-end argument: some functions can only be implemented correctly at the endpoints
Predict why putting reliability only in the network still leaves the endpoints checking

concepts.name: Bandwidth-delay product
concepts.summary: How much data fits in the pipe.
objectives: Define the bandwidth-delay product as how much data fits in the pipe
Predict why a sender must keep that much data in flight to fill a long fat path

concepts.name: Ethernet frames
concepts.summary: A local delivery envelope with a MAC address.
objectives: Describe an Ethernet frame as a local delivery envelope with MAC addresses
Distinguish a frame that stays on a local link from a packet that can leave the network

concepts.name: MAC addresses
concepts.summary: A link-scoped interface name, not an Internet name.
objectives: Explain a MAC address as a local hardware name that is not an Internet name
Predict why two hosts on different networks can reuse the same MAC without colliding on the Internet

concepts.name: Switching
concepts.summary: Learning which port a MAC last spoke from.
objectives: Describe a switch as learning which port a MAC last spoke from
Predict which port a frame takes once the switch has seen the destination speak

concepts.name: ARP
concepts.summary: Who has this IP? Tell this MAC.
objectives: Explain ARP as asking who has this IP and learning the MAC that answers
Predict why a host must resolve the next hop's MAC before it can send an IP packet on Ethernet

concepts.name: Shared versus switched media
concepts.summary: Collision domains did not vanish; they moved.
objectives: Contrast a shared medium where stations contend with a switched link that isolates collisions
Predict why a collision domain can still exist on Wi-Fi after Ethernet became switched

concepts.name: IPv4 addressing
concepts.summary: A hierarchical name the routers understand.
objectives: Describe an IPv4 address as a hierarchical name routers use to forward
Trace how a packet's destination address, not a MAC, decides the next network hop

concepts.name: CIDR and prefixes
concepts.summary: A length, not a class.
objectives: Explain a prefix as an address plus a length, not a class
Apply a prefix length to decide whether two addresses share a network

concepts.name: ICMP
concepts.summary: Control messages: unreachable, too big, echo.
objectives: Describe ICMP as control messages about reachability, size, and echo
Predict which ICMP message a hop sends when it cannot forward or the packet is too big

concepts.name: MTU
concepts.summary: The largest packet this hop will accept.
objectives: Define the MTU as the largest packet this hop will accept
Predict what happens when a packet is larger than the next hop's MTU

concepts.name: Fragmentation
concepts.summary: Splitting a packet the next link will not take — and why we try not to.
objectives: Explain fragmentation as splitting a packet the next link will not take
Predict why we try to avoid fragmenting and what fails if a fragment is lost

concepts.name: NAT, first look
concepts.summary: Many private addresses sharing one public one.
objectives: Describe NAT as many private addresses sharing one public address via a mapping
Predict why an unsolicited inbound packet has no table entry to land on

concepts.name: Network byte order
concepts.summary: Big-endian on the wire, whatever you are at home.
objectives: Explain network byte order as big-endian on the wire regardless of the host
Predict what a little-endian host must do before a multi-byte header field is sent

concepts.name: Checksums
concepts.summary: A cheap detector, not a cryptographic proof.
objectives: Describe a checksum as a cheap detector of accidental change, not a cryptographic proof
Predict what a receiver does when the checksum does not match

concepts.name: UDP
concepts.summary: A port number and a hope.
objectives: Describe UDP as a port number on top of IP with no delivery promise
Predict what an application must do itself if a UDP datagram is lost

concepts.name: The socket API
concepts.summary: How a process binds a port and exchanges bytes.
objectives: Describe the socket API as how a process binds a port and exchanges bytes
Trace bind, send, and receive as the process-visible interface to the stack

concepts.name: DNS, first look
concepts.summary: Names that resolve to addresses.
objectives: Explain DNS as a name that resolves to an address
Predict why a program that only has a name must ask before it can send an IP packet

concepts.name: DHCP
concepts.summary: Borrowing an address for a while.
objectives: Describe DHCP as borrowing an address and related config for a lease
Predict what a host lacks if it never hears a DHCP offer
